0.text: The process starts with start and immediately proceeds to Receive production order, after which Prepare materrials is carried out and then Assemble door. From there, the flow enters a loop that initiates a quality cycle: it continues with Send inquiry for quality check, followed by Receive inquiry for quality check, then Check quality, after which Send quality report is performed and the result is taken in at Receive quality report. Based on this, a decision is made at D1: if issues are found, Fix door is executed and the flow returns to the same loop entry to repeat the quality cycle (Send inquiry for quality check → Receive inquiry for quality check → Check quality → Send quality report → Receive quality report → D1) until the door passes; if the door is acceptable, Release door is performed, after which the flow converges at Post-D1 merge and the process ends at end.

1.text: The process starts and proceeds to Receive production order, then continues with Prepare materrials and Assemble door. From there, the flow enters a loop that leads to Send inquiry for quality check, after which the inquiry is received in Receive inquiry for quality check, the product is evaluated in Check quality, and the outcome is communicated in Send quality report. The report is then handled in Receive quality report, where a decision is made: if issues are found, the path goes to Fix door and then returns to the loop so that the quality-check cycle (from sending the inquiry through receiving the report) is repeated; if everything is acceptable, the path instead goes to Release door, after which the process ends.

2.text: The process starts and the production order is received, after which materials are prepared and the door is assembled. An inquiry for a quality check is then sent, which is received by the quality function; they perform the quality check, compile the quality report, and send it back. The report is received and assessed: if issues are identified, the door is fixed and the inquiry for a quality check is sent again, repeating the quality check cycle until the report indicates no issues. When the report is satisfactory, the door is released and the process ends.

3.text: The process begins with receiving the production order, followed by preparing materrials and assembling the door. If the result is “Acceptable, release,” the door is released and the process ends.

If Release door is selected, the flow proceeds to D1 Merge and the process ends.

0.text: The process starts when a shipment request is received. Immediately, two strands of work begin in parallel: the goods are packaged, and in parallel the kind of shipment is selected. Once the shipment type is chosen, one of two paths is followed. If a carrier-based shipment is chosen, quotes are requested from carriers, a carrier is assigned, and the shipment paperwork is prepared. Alternatively, if a postal shipment is chosen, a post label is filled in and the insurance is checked; if the existing insurance is sufficient the process proceeds, otherwise extra insurance is taken out before continuing. These shipment-preparation paths rejoin, and only when both the shipment preparation and the packaging have been completed does the process continue. The paperwork is then added to the package, the package is moved to the pickup area, and the process ends.

1.text: The process starts with start, after which Receive shipment request is carried out. The work then proceeds in two concurrent tracks: on one track, Package goods is performed; on the other, Select kind of shipment is executed. From the selection, a decision leads to two simultaneous strands of work. In the first strand, Request quotes from carriers is performed, followed by Assign a carrier, and then Prepare paperwork. In the second strand, Fill in a post label is completed, then Check insuarance is performed, after which a decision is taken: either continue directly without extra coverage, or take out additional coverage by executing Take out extra insuarance; in both cases this strand converges afterward. Once both strands stemming from the selection have completed, they rejoin. In parallel with that, the packaging track finishes, and only when both the packaging and the selection-related work are done does the process continue. Next, Add paperwork is carried out, then Move package to pickup area follows, and the process concludes with end.

0.text: The process starts by getting a travel request, after which a tour plan is prepared and then sent. A response is received, and a decision is made whether to proceed. If proceeding, the tour is booked and the customer is charged. After charging, another decision determines whether to contact the customer or to send the bill; whichever of these two occurs, the flow continues to send the booking confirmation. Following the confirmation, a further decision either loops back to repeat the charging stage (and thus the subsequent choice between contacting the customer or sending the bill, followed again by sending the booking confirmation) or exits the loop to completion. If, after receiving the response, the decision is not to proceed, the process skips booking and ends directly.

1.text: The process begins with receiving a travel request, after which a tour plan is prepared and sent. A response is then received and, depending on that outcome, the process either proceeds to book the tour or ends immediately. If the tour is booked, the customer is charged and a decision is made to either contact the customer or send the bill; whichever of these two is performed, the process then continues by sending the booking confirmation. After the confirmation is sent, a decision is made whether to repeat the charging-and-notification cycle or to finish. If it repeats, the flow returns to charging the customer, followed by either contacting the customer or sending the bill, merging back to send another booking confirmation and revisiting the same decision again. When repetition is no longer needed, the flow moves to completion and the process ends.

2.text: The process starts when a travel request is received. The tour plan is prepared and then sent, after which a response is received. Based on that response, either the case is closed immediately, or the tour is booked. If it proceeds, the customer is charged, and then either the customer is contacted or the bill is sent. After that, a booking confirmation is sent. At this point, a decision is made: either another charging cycle is performed—returning to charge the customer and then again either contacting the customer or sending the bill followed by another booking confirmation—or the process is concluded. When it is concluded, it reaches the same completion point as the early-closure path and ends.

3.text: The process starts by getting a travel request, then preparing the tour plan, sending the tour plan, and receiving the response. Based on that response, either the process proceeds directly toward completion or it continues with booking the tour. If it continues, booking the tour is followed by a cycle: the flow enters a loop in which the customer is charged, after which either the customer is contacted or the bill is sent, both leading to sending a booking confirmation. After the confirmation, either the loop repeats from charging again or the cycle ends and the process moves on toward completion. If the earlier response led directly to completion, or once the booking and any repeated charging/confirmation cycles are finished, the process concludes. There are no cross-participant communications.

4.text: The process starts when a travel request is received. The request is first reviewed to prepare the tour plan, which is then sent out. A response is awaited, after which a decision is made: either proceed with arranging the tour or conclude the process. If proceeding, the tour is booked and the customer is charged. Next, another decision determines how to follow up: either the customer is contacted, or a bill is sent followed by a booking confirmation. These alternatives rejoin, and a check is made whether another charging cycle is needed; if so, the process returns to charging and repeats the same follow-up decision and actions. If no further charging is required, the process concludes. If, after the initial response, the decision is not to proceed with arranging the tour, the process ends immediately.

5.text: The process starts when a travel request is received. The tour plan is prepared, then sent, and a response is received. After charging, a further choice is made: either the customer is contacted, or a bill is sent and, afterward, a booking confirmation is sent. In either case, the process then proceeds to completion.

6.text: The process starts with getting a travel request, after which a tour plan is prepared, sent, and its response is received. Based on that response, either the process proceeds directly to completion, or the tour is booked. If the tour is booked, a control step determines whether to continue with post-booking activities; if so, the customer is charged and a choice is made between two alternative follow-ups: either the customer is contacted, or a bill is sent followed by a booking confirmation. After either alternative, the flow returns to the control step, which can repeat the charge-and-notify cycle or decide to finish. When the control step decides to finish, the process proceeds to the final consolidation and ends.

7.text: The process starts, a travel request is obtained, the tour plan is prepared, the plan is sent, and a response is received. Depending on that response, either the tour is booked or the process is concluded immediately. If the tour is booked, the flow enters a cycle: the customer is charged, and then, based on the outcome, either the customer is contacted before proceeding, or the bill is sent followed by a booking confirmation. After completing whichever of these two branches applies, the flow either repeats the cycle (returning to the charging step for another iteration) or exits the cycle to conclude the overall process.

8.text: The process begins with receiving a travel request, after which a tour plan is prepared and then sent. A response is received and evaluated: either the process proceeds with booking or it is concluded without booking. If it continues, the tour is booked and the customer is charged. After charging, a decision is made between two alternatives: either the customer is contacted, or the bill is sent and then a booking confirmation is sent. Both alternatives lead to a checkpoint where the outcome is reviewed: either the process loops back to repeat the charging step (allowing for another attempt or adjustment), or it moves on to the final consolidation point and the process ends. If, right after the response is received, the decision is not to proceed with booking, the process moves directly to the final consolidation point and then ends.

9.text: The process starts, then Get travel request is carried out, followed by Prepare the tour plan and then Send the tour  plan. Next, Receive response takes place, after which a decision is made: either proceed with Book the tour or skip directly toward completion. If Book the tour is chosen, the process enters a cycle where Charge  customer is performed and then a choice is made between two branches. One branch carries out Contact customer before rejoining, while the other branch performs Send the bill and then Send booking confirmation before rejoining. After these actions rejoin, the process may either repeat the cycle starting again at the same loop entry (to perform another Charge  customer and subsequent branch) or proceed to conclude the booking path and rejoin the earlier decision that followed Receive response. Finally, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts and the patient is first diagnosed with non specific low back pain. Based on this, one of two alternative nonpharmacological approaches is chosen: either superficial heat or another nonpharmacological treatment is applied, or exercise or another nonpharmacological treatment is applied. If the superficial heat/other nonpharmacological route is taken, after completing it there is a decision whether to prescribe an NSAID or a skeletal muscle relaxant; if that prescription is made, it is carried out, otherwise this step is skipped, and in either case this path then proceeds to rejoin the main flow. If instead the exercise/other nonpharmacological route is taken, after completing it there is a decision whether to prescribe an NSAID; if an NSAID is prescribed, it is carried out and followed by another decision on whether to prescribe an opioid; if an opioid is prescribed, it is carried out, otherwise that step is skipped; if no NSAID is prescribed, both prescriptions are skipped. This path then also rejoins the main flow. After the chosen path completes and all optional prescriptions on that path are either executed or skipped, the process ends.

0.text: The process starts when a customer request is received and then checked. Based on this check, either the case is handled by informing the customer and finishing, or it proceeds with processing. If it proceeds, a choice is made between performing a manual registration or an automatic registration; once the selected registration is completed, a search for an attraction provider is carried out. At this point, either the booking step is skipped and the flow continues, or an attraction is booked. If a booking is attempted, the outcome leads to either receiving a rejection or receiving a booking confirmation; in either case, a confirmation is then sent to the customer. After either skipping the booking or sending the confirmation following a booking outcome, the flow rejoins and a decision is made whether to repeat the search cycle: if repetition is needed, the process returns to searching for an attraction provider; otherwise, the processing branch concludes and the overall process completes.

1.text: The process starts, the request is received from the customer and then checked. Based on this check, either the customer is notified and the process ends, or the request proceeds to registration. If it proceeds, registration is performed either manually or automatically, after which an iterative cycle begins. In each cycle, a search for an attraction provider is carried out. If a suitable provider is available, the attraction is booked; this can result either in a rejection being received or in a booking confirmation being received. When a rejection is received, the process may continue with another search-and-book attempt or leave the cycle. When a booking confirmation is received, a confirmation is sent to the customer and the cycle is completed. Leaving the cycle concludes the process.

2.text: The process starts when a customer request is received and then checked. Based on this check, either the customer is notified immediately and the process concludes, or the request proceeds to registration, which can be carried out manually or automatically; regardless of which option is chosen, the flow continues identically. Next, a search is conducted for an attraction provider. At this point, either the flow proceeds directly towards completion without attempting a booking, or a booking is made with the selected provider. If a booking is attempted, the outcome can be either a rejection or a booking confirmation; in both cases, the result is handled and a confirmation is sent to the customer. After sending this confirmation, a decision is taken whether to repeat the search-and-booking cycle for another provider or to stop iterating. If repetition is needed, the process returns to searching for a provider and follows the same steps again; otherwise, it exits the booking stage. Finally, the process joins back with any path that notified the customer right after the initial check and then ends.

3.text: The process starts when a customer request is received and then checked. Depending on the outcome of this check, either the customer is notified and the process ends, or the request proceeds to registration. If it proceeds, the registration is performed either manually or automatically, and once completed the process continues into a repeated search cycle. In this cycle, an attraction provider is sought, after which a decision is made whether to attempt a booking. If no booking is attempted, the search repeats. If a booking is attempted, the booking is made and the outcome is awaited: either a rejection is received or a booking confirmation is received. In both cases, a confirmation is then sent to the customer. Sending this confirmation ends the search cycle, after which the process concludes.

If a booking is made, the outcome is either a rejection or a confirmation: in case of rejection, it is received and the flow continues; in case of confirmation, the confirmation is received and then sent to the customer, after which the paths rejoin. After the search, either the process attempts to book the attraction or it skips directly toward concluding this part. If booking is attempted, the attraction is booked and then either a rejection is received or a booking confirmation is received; in either case, a confirmation is sent to the customer, after which this branch is concluded and rejoined with the path that skipped booking.
